name: QR code
purpose: Show a string as a machine-readable square so a second device can pick it up — a link, a reference, an enrolment code. The component's whole job is to stay SCANNABLE: real modules at a real size, with the quiet zone carried inside the artwork, and the same content repeated as text for anyone who is not going to point a camera at a screen.
$provenance-note: NEW at #210 (wave 4, lane B) against the wave-4 heavy-7 fan-out brief. Verified absent first-hand at build: `ls knowledge/snippets/ | grep -i qr` -> 0; `ls knowledge/components/ | grep -i qr` -> 0; `grep -rli qr knowledge/snippets/` -> 0.
$encoding-note: EVERY MATRIX IN THE SNIPPET IS A REAL ISO/IEC 18004 SYMBOL AND WAS DECODE-VERIFIED BEFORE THE FILE WAS WRITTEN. They were produced by a byte-mode encoder written for this lane (Reed-Solomon over GF(256), the four masking penalty rules, BCH(15,5) format information) and each was read back with OpenCV's QRCodeDetector; the build script REFUSES to emit a symbol that does not decode to its own stated payload. Symbol A encodes 'https://www.hsbc.co.uk/' (version 2, ECC M, mask 6, 25x25 modules). Symbol B encodes 'Pay 250.00 GBP to Acme Ltd ref INV-2291' (version 3, ECC M, mask 2, 29x29 modules). Both payloads are printed in the page beside their symbol. The brief's fence was explicit that a plausible-looking fake was the worst possible outcome; the verification is a known-answer decode, not an eyeball.

props.name: value
props.$note: The encoded string. It determines the symbol VERSION and therefore the module count: 23 characters gives a 25x25 version-2 symbol, 39 characters a 29x29 version-3 one. The component cannot be given a fixed module count.

props.name: size
props.$note: A MODULE size, not a box size: 4px, 8px and 12px per module. The pixel box is derived (module size x unit count) and never typed. Two payloads of different lengths at the same size are physically different sizes, and that is correct.

props.name: theme
props.$status: PROPOSED #210, Dave's eye owed — see accessibility.$openQuestion. Both are drawn side by side in section 4 of the snippet so the difference can be seen rather than argued about.

props.name: errorCorrection
props.$note: UNRULED. M is used throughout. The level trades symbol size against damage tolerance; a centre logo or lockup would REQUIRE level H and is not drawn here.

props.name: quietZone
props.$note: In MODULES, and it is inside the viewBox, not padding around it. Four is the ISO/IEC 18004 minimum. It is not exposed as something a consumer should reduce; it is a prop only because the number should be visible rather than buried.

variants.name: fixed-plate
variants.use: The symbol keeps a white plate and dark modules in every theme, because it binds mode-invariant tokens (surface/digital-black on text/reverse — the same hex in light and dark). Dark-on-light is what ISO/IEC 18004 specifies and what every reader handles.

variants.name: follows-theme
variants.use: The symbol binds the page's own text and background, so it inverts in dark mode: light modules on a dark field. Visually calmer inside a dark surface; tolerated by many modern scanners and not by all of them.

tokens.module-fixed: surface/digital-black — #1A1A1A in BOTH modes, which is the point
tokens.caption: text/default
tokens.$mono: MONO ONLY. No colour is bound anywhere in this component. The two-red law (s151-D1) and the mono error-ink camp (s149-D1) are untouched, and no RAG token appears in the file.
tokens.$sizing: --qr-mod 4px / 8px / 12px per module. The box is calc(--qr-mod * --qr-units), where --qr-units is the symbol's modules plus 8 (four quiet-zone modules each side).

commonPatterns: scan to open on another device

$relatedComponents: Payment-card-visual is the other 'a real artefact rendered in the UI' component in the library. The two share the discipline that the drawing must be TRUE, not merely plausible; nothing here adjudicates whether they belong to a family.

accessibility.roles: role="img" with an aria-label that says what the code is FOR, not what it looks like. The matrix itself is decorative to assistive technology — the payload is what matters and it is carried in text.
accessibility.keyboard: Nothing focusable in the symbol. Where the payload is a URL, the accompanying link is a real focusable anchor with the standard focus ring.
accessibility.announcements: None. A QR code that announces its own module count is noise.
accessibility.states: None. This is a static artefact.
accessibility.textAlternative: MANDATORY, not a nicety. A QR code is a sighted-and-has-a-second-device channel. Every specimen carries a figcaption stating the encoded string, and every URL payload also appears as a working link. A code with no text equivalent excludes the reader who cannot see it, the reader with one device, and the reader whose camera will not focus.
accessibility.$openQuestion: WHAT SHOULD A QR CODE DO IN DARK MODE? Both answers are drawn, and #210 MEASURED the difference rather than arguing it: as rendered in dark mode, the fixed-plate variant decoded and the theme-following variant did not (see $render-verification). Fixed plate keeps a white plate in every theme - always readable, but a bright square inside a dark surface. Theme-following is visually calmer and is what a dark UI wants to look like. This is a product-risk decision as much as a visual one, and it is Dave's.
accessibility.$secondOpenQuestion: WHICH PAYMENT-QR STANDARD, IF ANY? Symbol B in the snippet is a PLAIN-TEXT DEMONSTRATION STRING and is deliberately NOT an EPC/SEPA payload. Which standard a payment QR carries is a real product question and was not this lane's to pick.

antiPatterns: Inventing the matrix. A QR code that is a plausible texture rather than a real encoding is worse than no QR code: it looks finished, it passes every visual review, and it fails silently in the reader's hand.

Cropping the quiet zone. Four modules of clear margin are part of the symbol. Putting the matrix flush inside a padded card, or letting a container tighten around it, is the most common way a design-system QR code stops working.
Fixing the outer pixel box across payloads. A longer string means more modules; at a fixed box the modules shrink until the camera cannot resolve them. Size the MODULE, let the box follow.
Shipping without a text alternative. The code alone excludes anyone who cannot see it or has only one device.
Dropping a logo into the middle without raising error correction to H. The symbol may still scan on the phone it was tested on and fail on the next one.
Rounding the modules or adding a gradient for style. Both eat the contrast the decoder depends on, and neither is measured by any gate in this repo.

tokenValidation.result: PASS — 10 declared vars resolve in both light and dark; 2 declared contrast pairs clear their thresholds in both modes (snippet gate: 108 snippet(s), 0 failure(s)). surface/digital-black on text/reverse measures 16.1:1 and does not change between modes.
tokenValidation.$scope: MONO base only. Console, Legacy and Supercharge are NOT measured by this file and were NOT rendered by this lane. The fixed-plate variant is the one most likely to survive a theme unchanged, because its two tokens are mode-invariant — but that is an argument, not a measurement.

provenance.$note: Wave-4 heavy-7 fan-out (notes/_briefs/2026-08-20-210-wave4-heavy7-fanout-brief-v1.md), lane B. No Figma node.

$render-verification: DRIVEN AT #210, NOT ASSERTED. Every specimen was screenshotted AS THE BROWSER PAINTED IT (headless Chromium, file://, real HSBC face) and the pixels were fed back to OpenCV 5.0.0's QRCodeDetector. LIGHT: 6 of 6 sampled specimens decoded to their stated payload (default 264px, small 132px, large 396px, fixed-plate, theme-following, and the 296px version-3 payload). DARK: 5 of 6 decoded; THE THEME-FOLLOWING VARIANT RETURNED AN EMPTY STRING. Inverting those same pixels back to dark-on-light decodes them perfectly, so the failure is POLARITY and not content. One decoder is not every decoder - many phone cameras read inverted symbols - but this is a real reader failing a real render, and it is the strongest single input to the dark-mode question below.
